login.title: Sign in to AI-Biostat
login.intro: Pilot study: your participant code and password are issued by the teacher. No personal data needed.
login.passwordPh: 6 digits from the teacher or your own password
login.hint: Enter your participant code and password
login.tooMany: Too many attempts. Please wait 10 minutes

profile.title: Profile
profile.privacy: Your name is visible only to you and the teacher. Research exports use the code only.

password.title: Change password
password.intro: Set a password that is easy to remember — at least 6 characters, letters and digits allowed.
password.tooShort: New password must be at least 6 characters
password.done: Password changed. Use the new password next time you sign in.

diag.fullNote: (20 in the full version, variant A)
diag.note: Correct answers are not shown — this is an assessment, not an exam. You can close it and come back to this question.
diag.growth: Area for growth — “{{weak}}”. The tutor will ask more questions on this topic.

home.fillProfile: Add your name in the profile so the teacher can see whose work this is.
home.footer: All pilot cases contain training data only. The other 25 catalogue cases come after the pilot.

player.lockedNote: Method chosen: steps 1–4 are now read-only.
player.eduText: The data were simulated for this training task and contain no real information about patients, healthcare organisations or territories.

save.expired: Session expired — please sign in again
save.offline: No connection — answers will be saved when it is restored

tutor.title: AI tutor
tutor.blocked4: Answer on your own first — the tutor is not used at the “Question” step.
tutor.blocked7: You write the conclusion yourself. The tutor is not used at this step.
tutor.blocked8: Here you are checking an AI, so the tutor is not available.
tutor.intro: In the pilot the tutor opens in a separate tab. Your answers and scores are saved only here, in AI-Biostat.
tutor.how1: Copy a question below or ask your own
tutor.how3: Come back to this tab — your step is saved
tutor.askHere: What you can ask at this step
tutor.defaultQ: How should I approach this step?
tutor.counter: Tutor visits: {{n}} · counted in the study

step2.title: Step 2. Exploring the data
step2.intro: Check the data before the analysis. Click the rows that contain errors.
step2.why: Mark at least one row with an error

step3.title: Step 3. Variable types
step3.intro: Set the type of each variable and mark the outcome — what we are explaining.
step3.why: Set the type of all {{n}} variables and mark the outcome

step4.title: Step 4. Research question
step4.intro: State the research question and hypothesis in your own words. The tutor is not available at this step.
step4.label: Question and hypothesis
step4.why: Write at least one sentence (6+ words)

step5.title: Step 5. Choosing the method
step5.ok: Correct method. Once you move on, steps 1–4 become read-only.
step5.why: Choose a method and write a justification (5+ words)

step6.title: Step 6. Analysis in R or Python
step6.introPost: Write the analysis code yourself. The tutor can help with reference.
step6.introPre: Fill in the blanks in the template and run the code.
step6.phoneOnly: Only Python is available on a phone
step6.phoneNote: Only Python is available on a phone. We recommend a computer for this step: both R and Python are available there and coding is easier. Your work is saved — you can continue on a computer.
step6.otherLang: The other language ({{lang}}) opens for comparison after the case is finished.
step6.why: The code must run without errors

step7.title: Step 7. Interpretation
step7.intro: Write the conclusion in your own words. The tutor does not write it for you at this step.
step7.label: Your conclusion
step7.structure: Structure of the conclusion (no ready-made wording):

step8.title: Step 8. Critical check of AI
step8.intro: Another AI wrote a conclusion from these data. Click the fragment with an error and explain what is correct. The tutor is not available at this step.
step8.label: What is wrong and what is correct
step8.why: Choose a fragment and write a correction (5+ words)

step9.title: Step 9. Debriefing
step9.disputed: Disputed · the score is preliminary, you can continue
step9.dialogIntro: Your answer, the AI score and your arguments go to the study author or an assigned teacher. Until the decision the score is “disputed”, but you can keep learning. The decision and its justification will appear here.
step9.argumentPh: Why you disagree with the score

step10.title: Step 10. Case completed
step10.resultNote: , preliminary. You will be notified of the teacher's decision in the app and by e-mail.
step10.otherCode: The {{lang}} code is now available for comparison:
step10.note: The next case is not filled in the prototype — the button goes to the home page.

debrief.method1: Method chosen on the first attempt
debrief.method2: Method chosen on the second attempt
debrief.interpMissing: The conclusion is missing required elements

review.intro: Disputed scores first. A dispute does not block the student; they will see the decision and its justification.

people.footer: Exports contain participant codes only. The “code — name” table is kept separately by the study author.

import.title: Add participants
import.help: A CSV file from Excel with columns code;role;group;lang, e.g. P-1001;student;KZ-301;kk. Role: student, specialist or teacher. Language: kk, ru or en. No names — codes only. Existing participants are not changed.
import.passwordsHelp: Download the file and hand the passwords out. A lost password can be reissued with the “New password” button.

reset.confirm: The old password will stop working.

editor.intro: A case is published only after the key is checked by a biostatistician and the content by a medical education expert. The author decides on publication.
editor.newIntro: The draft is saved automatically. Before submitting for review you can open the case as a student.
editor.name: Title
editor.namePh: e.g. Missed ART doses and viral suppression
editor.situationPh: The learner's role and professional task
editor.dataHint: The “Training data” label is added automatically. Real names of territories and organisations are not used.

diagTab.intro: Two parallel variants of 20 items with the same structure: variant A — entry, variant B — final assessment.
diagTab.note: The distribution of items across competences is preliminary and approved by the author.
